proposals.before: When Emperor Fei first entered and took the throne, he asked Wang Mei, commissioner of the Three Departments: "How large are the treasury and granary holdings?"
proposals.after: When the Deposed Emperor first entered and took the throne, he asked Wang Mei, commissioner of the Three Departments: "How large are the treasury and granary holdings?"
proposals.reason: Chinese 廢帝 is rendered Deposed Emperor in s0000i but Emperor Fei here; standardize to Deposed Emperor.

proposals.before: Wenji had long been at odds with Chancellor Cui Xie. When Xie appointed a director in the Ministry of Works at Ye, Wenji flew into a rage because Ye was homophonous with his father's name. The appointee came to the ministry for his induction audience, but Wenji refused to receive him and took an extended leave.
proposals.after: Wenji had long been at odds with Chancellor Cui Xie. When Xie appointed Yu Ye as a director in the Ministry of Works, Wenji flew into a rage because Ye was homophonous with his father's name. When Ye came to the ministry for his induction audience, Wenji refused to receive him and took an extended leave.
proposals.reason: Chinese 於鄴 is the personal name Yu Ye, not the place Ye; the idiomatic English first treats Ye as a place then as a person.

decisions.reason: 廢帝 is the historiographic title 'Deposed Emperor,' not a personal or posthumous name to romanize as Emperor Fei.
於鄴 is the appointee Yu Ye's full name. The following clauses shorten it to 鄴 and describe his arrival and death, confirming that the phrase is not a locative construction.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 協除工部郎中於鄴……鄴赴省參上……鄴因醉忿自經死

claimRevisions.reason: 鄴 is Yu Ye's given name, not a second full personal name; classifying it correctly prevents a misleading one-word alias on his person page.
